text: For a *sentence* φ (no free variables) and a structure 𝓜, how does the truth of φ in 𝓜 depend on the variable assignment s?
choices: It depends critically on s; different assignments can flip φ between true and false
φ can only be evaluated after Skolemizing away all quantifiers
It is independent of s: 𝓜, s ⊨ φ holds for some s iff it holds for every s
s must map every variable to the same domain element
explanation: For a sentence the assignment s is irrelevant: 𝓜, s ⊨ φ holds for some s iff it holds for every s, which is why we may write 𝓜 ⊨ φ without mentioning s. Free variables (absent here) are what make truth assignment-dependent, so option 1 is wrong; options 2 and 4 are not requirements of the satisfaction definition.
